**Welcome back!** OpenAI's coding agents pushed so much code that the company rebuilt the machinery behind Git, three weeks after Anthropic ditched it. Sam Altman says the model that cracked a $1 million math problem is coming soon. Claude can now take 4x more data in one go. **In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

----------

## OpenAI rebuilt Git to keep up with Codex

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9ae37ce5-8a0b-4384-b649-719823faa4ba/bcb8b1b9-de65-4781-b113-f26c6688a4a5.jpg?t=1793692572)
Caption: 

Codex agents were pushing so much code that [OpenAI's Git servers started failing](https://openai.com/index/scaling-git-at-openai/), with reliability dropping below 90% at times.

So OpenAI built Pando, a new backend for Git, and it's been running since April.

Git is the tool almost every developer uses to save and share code. Three weeks ago, [Anthropic said Claude had outgrown it](https://www.anthropic.com/research/redesigning-source-control) and swapped it for a system of its own.

OpenAI's fix sits behind Git, so its engineers and agents didn't have to change a thing.

* Commits to OpenAI's main codebase are up 1,378% since early 2024, and it expects 2,442% by year's end.

* Pushing code is now about 5x faster, and Pando serves almost a petabyte of code a day.

* One engineer designed it and teams of Codex agents built it in 10 weeks.

* Anthropic's own post suggested companies rebuild Git's servers instead of leaving Git, which OpenAI had already done.

OpenAI says it's exploring ways to share the tech with its users.

81861.subject: The Super-Agent Blueprint: Building an Always-On, Production-Grade AI Agent 🤖
81861.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/deepseek-super-agent-blueprint

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
Most AI agents today fail because of the system wrapped around the model. DeepSeek [ https://substack.com/redirect/ff9b5d3b-17f0-49c8-bf4d-e96c8008aa05?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] has just published a blueprint for fixing that.
Today’s coding agents and personal assistants can finish a single task with little supervision. Yet they still live inside one chat session at a time, and the DeepSeek Harness team finds a person can follow only 3 to 5 active sessions at once. So agent productivity is now basically capped by human attention [ https://substack.com/redirect/6280a9fe-9ba7-4931-9fd3-212b3bd0539b?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ].
What is a Super-agent?
A Super-agent is a single, always-on AI agent that keeps one continuous memory across every channel, runs many tasks in parallel, acts on events without being prompted, and recovers from failures on its own. The closest thing to this we have today is probably SpaceXAI’s Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/fc6daf81-d276-4328-b8c9-0f853d28e433?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], the AI agent product we called the first real AI Agent OS.
But the exact term above comes from the DeepSeek Harness team’s paper Exploring Super-agent Design, which was just published. It describes the architecture behind their internal agent, which watches team chat, spots bugs nobody tagged it on, and opens pull requests to fix them.
That’s the gap between a demo and a Grok-bot-quality agent [ https://substack.com/redirect/79e4785f-de7d-44c2-87ed-74385b6cdbab?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]. You can tag it in any thread, and it answers fast, remembers the whole story, works while you sleep, and never needs a restart.
Why this architecture matters
First, the numbers that back it up. In DeepSeek’s preliminary tests, the Super-agent design finished tasks about 40% faster at the median than a standard single-session agent, and nearly halved the time its slowest 5% of tasks took. It also got more efficient as traffic grew: when load rose 40-fold, the inference time per routing decision fell by three quarters.
Then the delegation result worth remembering. Given a neutral prompt to use subagents when appropriate, a single-session agent never delegated once in five runs. Even a prompt that pushed hard for delegation failed once, so the fix has to be structural. And the best part is that because the design lives in the system around the model and borrows proven ideas from computer systems, it applies whether you build on DeepSeek, Claude [ https://substa

Binance reopened withdrawals over the weekend, starting with bitcoin on Sunday. By 7:36 a.m. ET that day, all 15 network groups in its first phase were open, and [U.S. dollar withdrawals came back today](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/binance-restores-usd-withdrawals-as-post-hack-reopening-expands). In the first nine and a half hours, customers withdrew $4.649 billion and deposited $1.01 billion, [Binance said](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-posts-4-54-billion-net-outflow-as-tracked-rivals-gain-564-million). It now says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen assets with its own funds. The rest are less-liquid tokens it is still buying. 

So far, Binance has covered the loss with its own money, without counting the frozen funds. On Friday, we wrote that Binance's [$6.34 billion reserve](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-it-has-reserved-over-6-34-billion-to-cover-hack-losses) covered the estimated $6.3 billion loss before any frozen funds came back. Only $5 billion of it was held in the stolen tokens, about 80% of the loss. Binance closed most of that gap in three days. It reported [90% replaced on Saturday](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-90-of-stolen-assets-replenished-targets-nov-1-restart) and 95% on Sunday. To get there, it drew on its corporate treasury and part of its futures insurance fund. Binance says what remains in that fund still exceeds the coverage its risk framework requires.
